title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV cache (CrestPay)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked CrestPay through Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and prefix/KV caching. Discussed expected cost savings, latency tradeoffs, deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), and SOC2/KMS concerns. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot: benchmarking live traffic with Redwood's autotuner and a shared cost model spreadsheet.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet and Optimize config template
CrestPay to provide 3 sample traffic traces and a sample prompt set
Schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff with infra team next week
SE to propose preliminary batching + cache profile within 48 hours
action_items: Ivy Chen - Share cost model spreadsheet and link to Optimize docs (due: 2026-04-13)
Raj Patel - Prepare initial batching / kv-cache profile and recommended autoscaler settings (due: 2026-04-13)
Derek Shaw - Upload 3 representative traffic traces to shared folder and confirm VPC requirements (due: 2026-04-14)
Laura Gomez - Provide 20 canonical prompts and success criteria for quality regression checks (due: 2026-04-14)
transcript:
00:00 Laura Gomez: Okay, I think we're all set. Hi Ivy, hi Raj, thanks for doing this.
00:06 Ivy Chen: Hey Laura, thanks for carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Ivy, AE at Redwood, and Raj is our solutions engineer who will go deep on Optimize.
00:13 Raj Patel: Hey everyone. Quick call plan — we'll walk through batching, prefix vs KV cache, cost model, and then Q&A, then next steps.
00:22 Priya Menon: Sounds good. We're especially interested in token costs and tail latency for the chat flows.
00:28 Ivy Chen: Got it. Derek, do you want to confirm infra constraints?
00:32 Derek Shaw: Sure. We're running on GCP, us-west1, GKE, and we prefer VPC private peering. We can do hosted for initial POC but will likely move to Dedicated or Private. Also SOC2 is a hard requirement.
00:42 Raj Patel: Good to know. That lines up with customers we've seen. Alright, first slide — batching. There are two core modes we recommend: dynamic continuous batching and fixed-window batching. In our tests, dynamic gives best latency for spiky traffic, fixed can squeeze cost for very stable load.
00:58 Laura Gomez: Can you quantify? Like percentage improvement?
01:02 Raj Patel: Sure. For typical request sizes (avg 140 tokens), dynamic batching with a 4-8ms queue window gave 20-30% cost reduction vs naive single-request serving, while keeping P95 under 220ms on A100-class instances. For fixed window at 50ms and larger batch sizes we saw up to 45% savings but tail P99 jumped to 450-600ms in some setups.
01:25 Priya Menon: So there's a tradeoff — cost vs tail. Our product team needs P95 < 300ms for chat. P99 can be higher but we need predictable SLOs.
01:34 Raj Patel: Exactly. Redwood Optimize autotuner picks queue windows and batch thresholds to meet your P95 target while maximizing token throughput. We'll show the spreadsheet with modeled unit economics in a sec.
01:45 Derek Shaw: What about concurrency limits and KV cache memory? We have a 256GB GPU pool per node.
01:50 Raj Patel: KV cache memory depends on model size and sequence lengths. For a 70B model and avg seq 1024, the KV footprint per concurrent request is roughly X — sorry, let me rephrase: around 1.2-1.6 GB per concurrent session with full KV. With prefix caching enabled, if many sessions share identical prefixes, effective memory per session drops dramatically.
02:11 Laura Gomez: Prefix vs KV — can you clarify use cases?
02:14 Raj Patel: Sure. Prefix cache is best when you have repeated system or user prompts — e.g., templated system messages, canned instructions, or shared conversation starters. It stores the cached tokenization and partial KV so repeated prefixes skip forward compute. KV cache (per-session) stores decoded keys/values between tokens to avoid recomputing attention for previously generated tokens — important for long stateful conversations. Prefix is more beneficial for shared repeated text; KV is necessary for session continuity.
02:40 Priya Menon: In our payments chat, identical disclaimers and onboarding prompts are used a lot. Seems prefix cache would help.
:02:47 Raj Patel: Yes, you'll likely see large wins. In our benchmark with a payments customer — similar to CrestPay — enabling prefix cache removed ~35-50% of token compute on the prefix portion, yielding 18-28% total token-cost reduction after amortization.
03:03 Laura Gomez: Those are big numbers. How do we measure regression risk? We care about quality staying within a small delta.
03:09 Ivy Chen: Great question. We'll run A/B evals using your prompt set and our eval harness. We tie quality alerts in Optimize to per-prompt metrics; if the cached path changes output distribution beyond a threshold we flag it.
03:22 Derek Shaw: Anything we need to change in our prompts?
03:24 Raj Patel: Usually minimal. Best practice: mark stable system text explicitly so you can identify cached prefixes. We provide a small SDK helper to tag prefixes.
03:31 Priya Menon: On the cost model spreadsheet, what assumptions are you using for token pricing and GPU efficiency?
03:36 Raj Patel: We include token pricing for hosted API, reserved GPU hour costs for Dedicated, and an efficiency multiplier for batch throughput. For example, a 2x batching efficiency improvement is modeled as halving per-token GPU hours. We also model cache hit rate in three tiers: low(10-20%), medium(35-45%), high(60%+).
03:56 Ivy Chen: We'll attach the spreadsheet after the call — it's the same one we used in the demo — link will be in the follow-up.
04:02 Laura Gomez: Can you walk us through a concrete modeled example?
04:05 Raj Patel: Yeah — sample: 1M monthly requests, avg 140 tokens in, 60 tokens out. With no batching/no cache hosted costs were $X (placeholder), with dynamic batching + prefix cache at medium hit rates we model ~37% reduction, with dedicated reserved capacity the unit cost drops further but you need the commit. If you can commit predictable 3-6 months of throughput, Dedicated pays off.
04:28 Derek Shaw: What's the adjustment for tail latency on dedicated GPUs?
04:31 Raj Patel: Dedicated pools give lower and more predictable queueing. With dedicated GPUs and continuous batching, your P95 improved by 30-40% vs shared hosted under bursty load. The autotuner respects your latency SLO and will prioritize smaller queue windows during high percentiles.
04:47 Priya Menon: Security — SOC2, KMS integration, logs/data residency? We need to know where token data is stored and for how long.
04:55 Ivy Chen: For Hosted we retain logs per your retention policy; we offer customer-managed keys via KMS for Private deployments; Dedicated can sit in your VPC with private peering to remove egress. SOC2 compliance and audit logs are available — we'll share security deck.
05:08 Laura Gomez: What about redwood's KV encryption at rest?
05:10 Raj Patel: KV cache on-host is encrypted at rest using your KMS if on Private. For Hosted, we have encryption at rest for data and configurable retention. We'll send the security pdf.
05:20 Derek Shaw: Ok. On the pilot — we want to run live traffic for two weeks. What's the minimum instrumentation?
05:25 Raj Patel: We'll need 1) traffic traces, 2) canonical prompts, 3) SLO targets (P95), and 4) a mapping of which prefixes are cacheable. We'll instrument cost and latency per-route and give you a config that can be toggled.
05:38 Laura Gomez: For the live traffic, any chance of quality drop during caching rollout? We worry about unseen prompts being miscached.
05:45 Raj Patel: Optimize uses a conservative cache warming policy: only cache prefixes that exceed a frequency threshold and pass a similarity check. We also support canary rollout and automatic rollback if quality metrics exceed thresholds.
05:58 Priya Menon: Great. Can you also run a short stress benchmark with our traffic shape and show the P95/P99 with and without cache?
06:04 Raj Patel: Yes — that's part of the pilot. We'll run both offline simulation and an online shadow run.
06:10 Ivy Chen: Recap — Redwood to share spreadsheet and Optimize config template, SE will prep initial profile, CrestPay to provide traces and prompts, then we do a 2-week pilot with canary.
06:20 Laura Gomez: Perfect. Anything else on pricing?
06:23 Ivy Chen: We'll put pricing scenarios in the spreadsheet: hosted per-token, Dedicated committed, and expected ROI from caching+batching. There may be discounts for multi-month reserved capacity.
06:34 Derek Shaw: One last infra question — does Redwood require special kernel drivers for batching improvements?
06:38 Raj Patel: No special drivers. The runtime uses optimized kernels and we select kernels at deploy time. For some quantized paths you might need NCCL/driver versions, we'll list those in the ops notes.
06:48 Priya Menon: Ok, that answers most of our questions.
06:51 Ivy Chen: We'll follow up with the spreadsheet, security deck, and a proposed pilot plan. Shall we aim to kick off next Wednesday?
06:58 Laura Gomez: Next Wednesday works.
07:00 Ivy Chen: Great — thanks everyone, we'll email next steps.
